understanding: Chapter 1 of 5: add a real `GeminiVlmProvider(VlmProvider)` at src/oko/providers/gemini_vlm.py that talks to Google Gemini's `generateContent` REST endpoint for model gemini-2.5-flash, plus an offline test file. It must mirror the existing http_vlm.py injectable-transport pattern so it imports without touching the network or filesystem, resolves its API key from GEMINI_API_KEY then a ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json (geminiApiKey) fallback, raises an honest RuntimeError naming the env var when no key exists anywhere, supports image input via request.image_b64 or image_path as inline_data, and parses candidates[0].content.parts[].text — raising RuntimeError rather than ever returning an empty/fake string. Explicitly out of scope: factory registration, triggers, pipeline wiring, demo (those are chapters 2-5), and any change to VlmGate/event architecture.
summary: Clone the structure and ergonomics of HttpJsonVlmProvider, swapping in Gemini specifics: per-query endpoint built from the model, x-goog-api-key header, contents/parts payload with snake_case inline_data, env->secrets key chain, and a strict candidates-parts text extractor. Keep the urllib transport as the production default and inject a fake transport in tests. Make the secrets fallback hermetically testable by isolating Path.home() so the 'no key' assertion is deterministic on any machine.

decision_atoms.statement: Reuse the exact http_vlm transport contract: HttpTransport = Callable[[url:str, payload:dict, headers:dict, timeout:float], dict], default to a module-level urllib POST helper, and inject it in tests.
decision_atoms.reason: The task says transport must be injected 'as in http_vlm.py'; reusing the identical 4-arg signature keeps test code shape-identical to the existing suite and gives offline determinism for free.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: The signature passes the already-built URL and headers, so the transport can't reshape the request; acceptable since Gemini's call is fully determined before the POST and matches the existing provider's boundary.

decision_atoms.statement: Build the endpoint at query time from self.model: f'https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent', and authenticate only via the x-goog-api-key header (Content-Type: application/json), with NO ?key= query param.
decision_atoms.reason: Contract and success_tests mandate this exact URL shape, the x-goog-api-key header, and gemini-2.5-flash as default; deriving the URL from self.model keeps model configurable while the default stays correct.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Header-only auth (vs the ?key= query form Google also accepts) means the key never lands in URLs/logs — strictly better — at the cost of diverging from some Google quickstart snippets.

decision_atoms.statement: Resolve the key strictly in query() with order: os.environ[api_key_env] (treat empty as absent) -> ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json field geminiApiKey -> RuntimeError mentioning api_key_env. Factor the secrets read into a module-level helper using Path.home().
decision_atoms.reason: Resolving only inside query() guarantees no network/FS at import (constraint); the env->secrets order and honest named error are explicit requirements; a separate helper keeps query() readable and lets tests isolate the fallback.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Touching the filesystem in the key path adds an FS dependency, but it's lazy (query-time only) and the helper centralizes it; the RuntimeError message must name the env var even though the failure also covers the secrets miss.

decision_atoms.statement: Make the secrets fallback hermetic in tests by monkeypatching Path.home() (or the helper) to a tmp dir, so the 'no key -> RuntimeError' case is deterministic regardless of a real ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json on the dev machine.
decision_atoms.reason: The build host plausibly has a real geminiApiKey in secrets.json (the secrets read was access-gated during exploration), which would silently break the negative test and even risk a live call; isolating home makes the test machine-independent.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Adds a small monkeypatch fixture and a minor coupling to the helper's home-dir lookup; the alternative (an injectable secrets_path arg) is cleaner but expands the public __init__ surface beyond what the contract asks.

decision_atoms.statement: Payload shape: contents=[{parts:[{text:prompt}] + optional [{inline_data:{mime_type,data}}]}]; emit the image part only when an image is present, preferring request.image_b64 over base64(image_path).
decision_atoms.reason: Matches the contract's contents/parts/inline_data spec and the existing provider's 'inline b64 wins over path' precedence; omitting the image part for text-only requests keeps payloads valid.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Uses REST snake_case (inline_data/mime_type) per the contract rather than the SDK's camelCase (inlineData/mimeType); correct for the generateContent REST endpoint but would break if anyone later swaps to the google-genai SDK transport.

decision_atoms.statement: _extract_gemini_text(raw) walks candidates[0].content.parts, concatenates every part['text'], and raises RuntimeError('Gemini response did not contain text') on any missing/empty/blocked path — never returns '' and never fabricates text.
decision_atoms.reason: Directly required: empty or malformed JSON (including safety-blocked responses with no candidates) must surface as an error, not fake text; concatenating parts handles Gemini's occasional multi-part splits.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: Strictness means a legitimately empty model answer also raises; acceptable for a security-monitoring VLM where a silent empty verdict is worse than a loud failure.

decision_atoms.statement: Default mime_type to 'image/jpeg', guessing from the image_path extension via mimetypes when a path is supplied (and optionally honoring request.metadata['mime_type']).
decision_atoms.reason: image_b64 carries no extension to infer from and OKO frames are JPEG, so a JPEG default is the safe baseline while path-based guessing improves correctness when available.
decision_atoms.tradeoff: A wrong default mime_type for non-JPEG inline_b64 could degrade Gemini's decoding; mitigated by the metadata override hook and path-based guessing, kept simple to stay within Chapter 1 scope.

decision_atoms.statement: Wrap only the transport call in time.perf_counter() to compute latency_ms and return VlmResponse(text=text, provider='gemini', model=self.model, latency_ms=...).
decision_atoms.reason: Mirrors http_vlm's timing and satisfies the VlmResponse field requirements (text/provider/model/latency_ms confirmed in domain/vlm.py).
decision_atoms.tradeoff: latency_ms measures wall-clock around the injected transport, so in tests it's near-zero/non-meaningful — fine, since determinism tests assert on payload/headers, not latency.

assumptions: VlmRequest exposes optional image_b64 and image_path, and VlmResponse takes (text, provider, model, latency_ms) — both verified in src/oko/domain/vlm.py.
The transport injection contract should match http_vlm.py exactly: (url, payload, headers, timeout) -> dict, with a urllib POST as the production default.

~/.bridge-private/secrets.json is a flat JSON object with a top-level string field geminiApiKey (slopvid google_auth pattern); a missing file or field is treated as 'no key', not a hard error before the RuntimeError.

The slopvid reference (literary-slop-video/slopvid/providers.py, google_auth.py) is NOT present in this repo, so the implementation follows the contract's documented Gemini shapes plus the in-repo http_vlm.py pattern rather than copying that file.
Default inline image mime_type of image/jpeg is acceptable for OKO frames; non-JPEG inputs are an edge case handled via path-based guessing/metadata override.
Factory registration and config-schema changes are intentionally excluded; the provider is constructed directly in tests, as in test_live_vlm_provider.py's direct HttpJsonVlmProvider construction.
Python's stdlib (os, json, base64, time, mimetypes, pathlib, urllib) is sufficient — no new third-party dependency is introduced.

risks.risk: A real geminiApiKey in ~/.bridge-private/secrets.json on the build machine makes the 'no key -> RuntimeError' test pass spuriously (or worse, encourages a live call), violating the deterministic/offline requirement.
risks.mitigation: Isolate the secrets lookup in tests by monkeypatching Path.home() to a tmp dir (or the secrets helper) for every negative-key case, and never let the urllib default transport run in tests — always inject a fake.

risks.risk: Using REST snake_case inline_data/mime_type is correct for generateContent but a future swap to the google-genai SDK (camelCase inlineData/mimeType) would silently send a malformed image part.
risks.mitigation: Keep payload construction in one private _payload/_gemini_inline_image helper with a comment pinning it to the v1beta REST contract, and assert the exact key names in tests so a shape regression fails loudly.

risks.risk: _extract_gemini_text could miss a response variant (e.g. safety-blocked promptFeedback with no candidates, or parts lacking 'text') and either crash with the wrong exception or, if written loosely, slip through as empty text.
risks.mitigation: Guard every access (candidates present & non-empty, content/parts are lists, part['text'] is a non-empty str after strip) and funnel all failure paths to the single RuntimeError('Gemini response did not contain text'); cover empty {}, missing-parts, and garbage shapes in parametrized tests.

risks.risk: Wrong default mime_type for base64 images with no path could degrade Gemini's image understanding without any error.
risks.mitigation: Default to image/jpeg (matching OKO frame encoding), guess from extension when image_path is given, and allow a metadata['mime_type'] override; document the default in the helper.

risks.risk: Scope creep into Chapter 2+ (factory wiring, triggers, config schema) would violate the 'do not run ahead' constraint and bloat the diff.
risks.mitigation: Limit the change to exactly two files (gemini_vlm.py + its test), construct the provider directly in tests, and leave a short module docstring noting that factory/pipeline integration is deferred to later chapters.

minimal_version: Add src/oko/providers/gemini_vlm.py with GeminiVlmProvider(VlmProvider): name='gemini', default model='gemini-2.5-flash'; __init__(model='gemini-2.5-flash', api_key_env='GEMINI_API_KEY', timeout_seconds=10.0, transport=None) doing only field assignment (no network/FS). query() resolves the key (env -> secrets.json geminiApiKey -> RuntimeError naming api_key_env), builds the per-model :generateContent URL, sets x-goog-api-key + Content-Type headers, assembles contents/parts with an optional inline_data image (b64 preferred, else base64 of image_path), times the injected transport for latency_ms, runs _extract_gemini_text over candidates[0].content.parts (RuntimeError on empty/missing), and returns VlmResponse(text, provider='gemini', model, latency_ms). Helpers _gemini_inline_image(request) and _extract_gemini_text(raw) as specified, plus a urllib POST default transport. tests/test_gemini_vlm_provider.py (offline, fake transport, Path.home isolated): asserts endpoint contains model and ':generateContent', x-goog-api-key carries the key, timeout is forwarded, both image_b64 and image_path yield inline_data with mime_type+data, no key anywhere raises RuntimeError matching 'GEMINI_API_KEY', and empty/garbage JSON raises RuntimeError (no fake text). Verify with a green pytest run.
advanced_version: All of the minimal version plus Chapter-1-scoped polish: mimetypes-based mime_type inference from image_path with an image/jpeg default and a request.metadata['mime_type'] override; multi-part text concatenation so split Gemini responses are joined rather than truncated; the secrets read factored into a small module-level helper (using Path.home()) that tolerates a missing file/field and is the single monkeypatch point in tests; an error message that, while still naming GEMINI_API_KEY, also notes the secrets.json path that was checked; and a tightened _extract_gemini_text that explicitly recognizes safety-blocked responses (no candidates / promptFeedback.blockReason) and still raises the exact 'Gemini response did not contain text' RuntimeError. Tests additionally cover: empty-string env var falling through to the secrets fallback, secrets.json supplying the key when env is unset, mime_type inferred from a .png path, and a multi-part candidate joining correctly. Deliberately excluded to honor the 'no running ahead' constraint: factory/config-schema registration, trigger logic, pipeline wiring, retries/backoff, and any live-network demo (deferred to Chapters 2-5).
